name: Online and offline state
plain: Tells the page whether the device believes it has a network.
meaning: Boolean only; true can still mean a captive portal or no internet. Events fire when the device loses or regains connection, revealing travel, elevators, flights.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can tell if your device thinks it is online, and when that changes
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens while the page is open and your connection changes
can: See a yes or no answer for being online
Notice when you lose or regain a connection
Switch to an offline mode and save your work for later
cannot: Know if the internet truly works, since a hotel login page still counts as online
See which network you are on
See your location, though repeated drops can hint you are on the move
Work after you close the tab
limits.reach_label: Yes or no, while page is open

story.what_it_is: A page knows whether your device thinks it is online, and gets told when that changes.

marketing.name: Navigator onLine
marketing.pitch: Pages can react when the device goes offline or comes back, for example to save work for later.

story.for_you: You may see a banner like You are offline, or a message that your changes will sync later. When the signal returns, the page catches up for you.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to protect user work, to switch to a saved copy and to retry actions. It is a simple signal, but it can be wrong, as a device can look online with no real internet.

use_cases.example: Google Docs shows Offline in the top bar when your signal drops, keeps your typing and syncs when you reconnect.
A browser game pauses and shows Reconnecting when the signal drops, then rejoins the match when it returns.
A web streaming app switches to downloaded titles when it sees the device is offline.
A chat site shows a clock icon on unsent messages while offline and sends them when back online.
A shop keeps a cart on the device when offline and syncs it when online.
A web design tool like Figma warns that edits are saved on this device only until a connection returns.
A news site shows saved articles while you ride through a tunnel.

technical_bounds: True means a link, not working internet
